sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a house in Andover, Minnesota?
sections.html:
An Andover owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. Each route ends the same way: a purchase agreement, a deed recorded with Anoka County, and a current tax picture for the buyer.

One rule applies whichever route you pick. Under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55, you must give the buyer a written disclosure before signing an agreement to sell residential property. It covers material facts you know that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the home, and it must be made in good faith. A seller may hand the disclosure to the buyer's licensed agent, which counts as delivery to the buyer.

A cash offer suits an Andover owner who wants a short timeline, has repairs waiting, or is dealing with an inherited house or tenants. Ask any buyer to put the price in writing, and check that the figure already accounts for tax owed and unpaid permits.

Andover is a city of about 33,874 people in Anoka County. The Census Bureau estimated that population for July 1, 2025, up 3.9 percent from the 2020 count of 32,601. The city covers about 34.8 square miles, and 22.9 percent of residents lived in areas the census classed as rural in 2020. The median age that year was 39.8, and 25.8 percent of residents were under 18.

The area was organized in 1857 as Round Lake Township and renamed Grow Township in 1860 after Representative Galusha Grow, who was prominent in passing the Homestead Act. Population stayed small for a century, at 757 in 1950 and 1,402 in 1960, and then jumped to 3,830 in 1970, 9,387 in 1980, 15,216 in 1990 and 26,588 in 2000, so most of the city's growth came after 1960.

County Roads 9, 18, 78 and 116 are the main routes, with U.S. Highway 10 close by. Crooked Lake, on the southern border and mostly inside Coon Rapids, is the only fully recreational lake. Most of Andover belongs to Anoka-Hennepin School District 11, whose schools inside the city include Andover Elementary, Crooked Lake Elementary, Rum River Elementary, Oak View Middle School and Andover High School. A small strip in the north belongs to St. Francis Area Schools, District 15, so check your address before you tell a buyer which district applies.

sections.html:
Andover is a city of owners, with a large share of long-term residents and big households. The table sets the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures for the city beside the national numbers.

In the 2020 census Andover had 11,005 housing units with a 2.0 percent vacancy rate, and 71.6 percent of households were married couples. These numbers describe the whole city, so a particular street can sit well above or below them.

sections.h2: Which Andover permits matter before I sell?
sections.html:
The Andover Building Department points out that work done without a required permit must be disclosed when a house is sold, and that code violations can slow or lower a sale. Before listing, compare your past projects against the city's permit list.

  • Permits are required for new construction, remodeling, additions and alterations, basement finishing, decks and porches, roofing, siding, irrigation systems and solid fuel fireplaces.
  • Plumbing permits cover water heaters and water softeners. Mechanical permits cover furnaces, air conditioners, boilers and gas fireplaces. Electrical work needs its own permit.
  • Septic systems need an installation permit and work by a Minnesota Pollution Control Agency licensed designer and installer. Pumping a septic tank takes a $20 permit that the pumper obtains.
  • No permit is needed for detached accessory structures under 200 square feet, sidewalks and patios, painting, flooring, cabinets, or normal maintenance such as replacing deck boards.

Homeowners may pull permits themselves, but the city says a licensed residential contractor is usually the better choice. Residential permits are typically approved right away or within one or two days. The Building Department is at 1685 Crosstown Blvd NW, reachable at 763-755-8700 or building@andovermn.gov.

Yes. Andover requires single family and multifamily rental housing to be licensed and inspected. Licenses run for two years, every rental home is inspected at least once within the term, and a license cannot be transferred to a new owner.

That last point matters if you are selling a rented house. A buyer who keeps the house as a rental needs a new license, so tell buyers early if the home is rented. The city's rental page links to Chapter 8 of the Andover ordinances and to the Minnesota Attorney General's landlord and tenant information.

sections.h2: How do Anoka County property taxes work when an Andover house sells?
sections.html:
Anoka County mails one tax statement per parcel each year, in mid-March. A change of ownership recorded after January 1 does not trigger a new mailing, so the statement goes to the previous owner or taxpayer, and the county can issue a duplicate on request. Not receiving a statement does not forgive a penalty.

Taxes are due May 15 and October 15, and the county says there is no grace period. If either date lands on a weekend, payment is due the next business day. You can pay at PayAnokaCounty with a card at 2.6 percent or an ACH e-check at $3.50, by mail to Anoka County Property Records and Taxation, 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, MN 55303, or in person at the Government Center in Anoka. The county's direct payment program, at 763-323-5400, withdraws payments automatically for free. Mail needs a postmark on or before the due date, and the county suggests asking a post office clerk for a hand-applied postmark.

Two sale steps are easy to miss. The owner must tell the assessor within 30 days when a homestead home sells, or the homestead is removed and penalties can follow. And a certificate of real estate value is filed with the county auditor under Minnesota Statutes section 272.115 when the deed is recorded. Proposed tax statements for next year arrive in mid-November, and they become final only after levies are approved in December.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Andover, MN?
faqs.a: Speed depends on the route. A cash buyer can often set a close date within the weeks you choose, while a listed sale depends on showings, financing and inspection. Whatever the route, you must still give the buyer the written seller disclosure before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a water heater in Andover?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a plumbing permit to replace a water heater or water softener. Furnaces and air conditioners need a mechanical permit.
Most of Andover is in Anoka-Hennepin School District 11. A small strip along the northern edge belongs to St. Francis Area Schools, District 15.

faqs.q: Who sends the Andover property tax statement?
faqs.a: Anoka County mails it, once a year in mid-March, and the county's Property Records and Taxation office takes payment. Call 763-323-5400 if you did not receive one.

faqs.q: Must I tell the county when I sell my Andover home?
faqs.a: Yes if the house was your homestead. Tell the assessor within 30 days of the sale, or the county may remove the homestead status and add penalties. A certificate of real estate value is also filed with the county auditor.
